clue.text: Feasts abroad, most free from risk

indicators.note: things sent abroad are scattered far from home, so the letters are moved out of their order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Banquets held overseas are the least hazardous kind of meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Safest is the superlative of safe, meaning least exposed to danger or harm.

clue.text: Bandage the man after violent blow

indicators.note: after places the man behind the blow, so the clue's later piece is written first

blocks.note: a swat is a sharp, hard hit
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A first-aider dresses the wound of a man who has taken a hard knock.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the man first, but 'after' puts him behind the blow in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap something up in cloth, as one does when binding a wound with strips.

clue.text: Reckon dignitary's not in

blocks.note: a public figure is a person of standing; the 's reads as 'is', joining it to what follows
the opposite of in

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that the important visitor is away from the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon something out, or figure it out, is to calculate or work out an answer.

clue.text: Withdraw with slight injury

blocks.note: first meaning: pull out of a race or contest before it starts
second meaning: a small surface wound

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls out of an event because of a minor knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor is scratched when taken out of an event, and a scratch is also a shallow graze.

clue.text: Film luminary was screening beginning of Rocky

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
to screen something is to hide it behind a cover, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a luminary is a celebrity, a star
taken as written
the first letter of Rocky

explanation.surface: A celebrity attended a showing of the opening of a boxing film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' and 'screening' both point to cinema, and Rocky is itself a film, so the surface stays on one subject while the parts do different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is George Lucas's 1977 science-fiction film and the series that grew from it.

clue.text: Clear river blocked by unruly US clan

indicators.note: an unruly crowd will not stay in line, so these letters are put in a new arrangement
a river blocked by something has that thing lodged in its middle

blocks.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An American family gang has dammed a waterway that was running clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' is usually just R, but here it is a whole named river that splits around the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Translucent material lets light through, so it is clear in the sense of not opaque.

clue.text: Procedure at home getting in the way

indicators.note: something getting in goes inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a route is a way to go
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A household procedure keeps getting in everyone's way.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, regular sequence of actions, which is what a procedure is.

clue.text: Invalidate yearbook, with article missing

indicators.note: missing means left out, so one letter standing for an article is removed

blocks.note: an annual is a book published once a year
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A school yearbook is declared void because a piece of writing is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it legally void, to invalidate it.

clue.text: Run out after dark in a Mexican's hat

indicators.note: after places the run out behind the dark word, so the clue's first piece goes second

blocks.note: sombre means dark or gloomy
cricket scorecards abbreviate a run out as r.o.

explanation.surface: Someone dashes outside at night wearing a Mexican hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out is a way a batter is dismissed in cricket. Sombre and sombrero share a Spanish root in sombra, shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is the broad-brimmed hat traditionally worn in Mexico to give shade.

clue.text: An artist holding shot rabbit

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the artist's letters go around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a go or a shot is an attempt

explanation.surface: A painter is carrying a rabbit someone has shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a hunting word next to rabbit, but it means an attempt, as in having a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of rabbit with long silky fur, also used to make wool.

clue.text: A blaze inside chimney in plant

indicators.note: inside means within, so these words are set within the chimney

blocks.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney
taken as written
to blaze is to burn

explanation.surface: A fire in a chimney sets light to a plant growing there.
explanation.definitionFit: Laburnum is a small tree with hanging yellow flowers, a plant common in gardens.

clue.text: Book had to include right dates

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one letter goes within the word

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
dates are fixed times

explanation.surface: A diary or ledger had to record the right dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is Charles Dickens's 1854 novel, so it is a book.

clue.text: Opera singer, Lanza, cut short La Scala broadcast

indicators.note: cut short means docked at the end, so the final letter is lost
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are spread into a new arrangement

blocks.note: Mario Lanza was an American tenor and film star
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A soprano and tenor Mario Lanza have a La Scala performance shortened on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Lanza is a surname, so the solver must supply his first name before docking it. La Scala is Milan's great opera house, which keeps the surface in the opera world.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Callas was the celebrated Greek-American soprano, one of the most famous opera singers of the twentieth century.

clue.text: One avoiding work, badly riled

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are in a faulty order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A shirker gets very angry and upset.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who spends time doing nothing, so one who dodges work.

clue.text: Dam lake for religious head

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
Lake Superior is the largest of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A reservoir is built with the water to serve a religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' looks like a barrier holding back the lake, but it is the word for an animal's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mother Superior is the nun in charge of a convent, its religious head.

clue.text: Fashionable German city church, basically

blocks.note: what is in is in fashion
Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A smart church in a German city is described in plain terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In essence means in its fundamental nature, so it is a phrase meaning basically.

clue.text: Summary of a bishop's religious pamphlet

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, and the possessive 's is kept as S
a tract is a short pamphlet, often on a religious theme

explanation.surface: Someone writes a précis of a bishop's devotional leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s usually just joins words, but here it is a letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short summary placed at the start of an academic paper.

clue.text: Similarly, purchase, say, an identical disc

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, so its sound stands for a differently spelt one

blocks.note: to purchase is to buy, which is spoken the same as the preposition
identical means the same
a token is a coin-like disc used in place of money

explanation.surface: Someone buys a matching coin, as before.
explanation.definitionFit: By the same token is an idiom introducing a parallel point, meaning similarly or for the same reason.

clue.text: Continually rest, heading off for mountain

indicators.note: a heading is the top or front, and taking it off removes the first letter

blocks.note: ever means always, continually
taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber keeps pausing for breath before setting off up the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, on the Nepal–Tibet border, is the world's highest mountain.

clue.text: Working daily? In theory

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person works every day, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' reads as an adverb about working hours, but it is a noun for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper is an idiom for what seems true in plans or theory but may not hold in practice.

clue.text: Origin of HP, perhaps, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is taken by its spoken sound

blocks.note: HP is a brand of brown sauce, the 'perhaps' marking it as one example

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the Hire Purchase or HP brand came from, by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a British brown condiment. In a non-rhotic British accent sauce and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A source is where something comes from, its origin or starting point.

clue.text: Take mouthful from ragout (a stew)

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the article and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A cook samples a spoonful of the casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to take a small mouthful to try its flavour.

clue.text: Angry about wife, used bad language

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the letter for the wife

blocks.note: sore is informal for angry or resentful
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man cross about his wife cursed.
explanation.definitionFit: Swore is the past tense of swear, to use profanity or offensive language.

clue.text: A new suggestion concerning an hors d'oeuvre

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tip is a helpful suggestion
as to means concerning

explanation.surface: Someone offers a fresh idea about a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is an Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables, the equivalent of an hors d'oeuvre.

clue.text: What 18 is especially?

definitions.note: a description of the mountain at 18, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: the mountain at 18 is the highest peak, standing over every other
second meaning: more than anything else

explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 18 is the world's highest mountain, so it stands literally higher than all others; the same phrase is an idiom for most importantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning more than anything, which is what especially means as an adverb.

clue.text: Key cricketer, first at the crease?

blocks.note: first meaning: a key is a tool that opens a lock
second meaning: the batter who starts an innings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key cricketer' reads as an important player; the comma splits it. The crease is the line where a cricket batter stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a device that opens things, and an opening batter is the first to go in for a cricket side.

clue.text: In stand is eastern paper

blocks.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A newspaper from the East is displayed on a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' looks like a noun, a newsstand, but it is the verb for paying for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper in the academic sense is a written study, and a treatise is a formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: Recited flourishing novelist

indicators.note: recited means spoken aloud, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: flourishing plants are green and lush

explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene wrote Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a twentieth-century English novelist.
